data.name: Grenada
data.summary: Grenada taxes residents only on Grenada-source income. There is no capital gains tax, no tax on dividends received by residents, and no inheritance, gift or net wealth tax, so a portfolio of foreign shares and bonds is effectively untaxed locally. Costs arise on Grenadian real estate (transfer tax up to 15%, 10% alien landholding licence). No treaty relief exists for US/EU withholding taxes.

regimes.name: Ordinary tax residence
regimes.description: Resident individuals are taxed only on income derived from Grenada (Deloitte 2026). There is no capital gains tax, no tax on dividends paid to residents, no inheritance, estate or net wealth tax.
regimes.eligibility: Tax residence: physical presence of at least 183 days in the fiscal year. Non-citizens need a residence permit or citizenship (see residency routes).

capital_gains.summary: Grenada has no capital gains tax. Gains on domestic or foreign shares, a private business or real estate are not taxed as gains. A real property transfer tax of 5% to 15% (paid by the seller) applies to sales of Grenadian land and buildings.
capital_gains.important_exceptions: Real property transfer tax 5%-15% (resident vs non-resident), payable by the seller on values above XCD 20,000. Non-resident (non-citizen) purchasers need an Alien Landholding Licence costing 10% of the property value.
open_questions: Deloitte describes the basis as Grenada-source only; the Income Tax Act text was not checked for any rule that taxes foreign income remitted to Grenada.
capital_gains.rate_basis: 0 = no capital gains tax (Deloitte Grenada Highlights 2026). Foreign gains are also outside the territorial income tax. The 5-15% real property transfer tax is a transaction tax on the seller and is not included in the real_estate_local rate.
capital_gains.professional_trader: Business income derived from Grenada is taxed at 10% / 28% (personal) or 28% (company). A resident who trades securities as a business in Grenada could in principle be treated as earning business income; no specific guidance was found.
capital_gains.foreign_assets: Income derived outside Grenada is outside the scope of personal income tax for residents.

dividends.summary: Dividends paid to residents are not taxed and carry no withholding tax. Foreign dividends are outside the territorial scope of personal income tax.
open_questions: No primary-law confirmation (Income Tax Act, Cap. 152) of the exemption for foreign dividends.
dividends.rate_basis: Deloitte Grenada 2026: 'Dividends paid to residents are not subject to tax'; residents are taxed on income derived from Grenada only.
dividends.withholding_outbound: 15% on dividends paid to non-resident companies and individuals, unless reduced by treaty. Interest and royalties: 15% to residents and non-residents.
dividends.treaty_network: Only the CARICOM multilateral tax treaty. No treaties with the US or EU states, so source-country withholding on US/EU dividends is not reduced and cannot be credited (no foreign tax relief).

wealth_tax.property_tax_note: Annual property tax on market value, 0% to 0.5% depending on use, with separate land and building rates; XCD 100,000 exemption on the building value of one owner-occupied home.

inheritance.summary: No inheritance, estate or gift tax. Gifts of Grenadian real property may attract the real property transfer tax.
inheritance.important_exceptions: Real property transfer tax may apply to gifts of Grenadian land; it does not apply to a portfolio of listed securities.
open_questions: Whether transfer tax applies to transfers of Grenadian real property on death (Deloitte mentions only gifts) was not verified.
inheritance.gift_tax: No gift tax. Deloitte notes that gifts may be subject to the real property transfer tax (transfers by deed above XCD 150,000).
inheritance.foreign_assets: No tax on foreign or local assets passing on death.

residency.tax_residency_test: Resident if physically present in Grenada for at least 183 days in a fiscal year (Deloitte 2026). Taxed on Grenada-source income only.

routes.name: Citizenship by Investment (CBI)
routes.requirements: Grenada operates a citizenship-by-investment programme (donation or approved real estate). Current minimum amounts were not verified in this research.

routes.name: Residence permit
routes.requirements: Non-citizens need a residence permit; conditions not researched.

corporate.summary: Corporate income tax 28%; resident companies (central management and control) are taxed on worldwide income. No capital gains tax, dividends paid to residents not taxed, no participation exemption or holding company regime. Grenada has not committed to Pillar Two.
corporate.special_zones: Incentives under the Fiscal Incentives Act, Qualified Enterprise Act and Hotel Aids Act.

data.us_citizen_notes: US citizens remain subject to US federal income, estate and gift tax on worldwide income and assets wherever they live; the app adds the federal layer. There is no local tax here to credit against US tax on portfolio income, so a US family pays the full US rates. No Puerto Rico-style exclusion applies.
open_questions: Current CBI investment thresholds not verified.

International/private secondary school fee for Grenada not sourced: re-checked 15 Oct 2026 (web search, Wayback Machine for Westmorland School, third-party listings): no Grenadian private secondary school publishes a fee schedule. Divine Savior Academy (St. George's) publishes 2026-27 fees but only for PreK-Grade 6 (international Kinder-Grade 6: EC$2,000 a term), so it was not used. A secondary fee schedule obtained from a school is needed.

income.name: Grenada

income_tax.summary: Income tax is 10% on the first XCD 24,000 and 28% above, after a XCD 36,000 personal allowance, and Deloitte states that residents are taxed only on income derived from Grenada. Employees pay 6.25% NIS up to XCD 5,000 a month.
income_tax.self_employed_notes: The 13.5% self-employed NIS rate and XCD 5,200 monthly ceiling (XCD 62,400 a year) come from a search-result summary of the NIS Grenada website, which could not be opened; unverified. Employee ceiling XCD 5,000 a month is Deloitte's.
income_tax.local_tax_note: No local income surtax. Deloitte 2026 states residents (183+ days) are taxed on income derived from Grenada, i.e. a territorial basis; no foreign tax relief; no capital gains tax. Brackets apply to taxable income after the XCD 36,000 allowance.
open_questions: The 13.5% self-employed NIS rate and XCD 5,200 monthly ceiling come from a search-result summary of the NIS website; the NIS sites (nisgrenada.org refused the connection, nisgrenada.com returned 403) could not be opened, so they remain unverified.
Third-party payroll sites quote different 2026 NIS shares (6.5% / 7.5%); Deloitte's 6.25% was used.
Allowance treatment (deducted before the 10%/28% bands) is inferred from the wording.

Grenada: whether the employee NIS contribution (6.25% per the NIS Grenada employer page) is deductible from taxable income could not be established: the PwC deductions page returns 404 and the Inland Revenue Division site (ird.gd) returned HTTP 500 on 2026-10-15. social_security_deductible left null.

regimes.name: Remote-work permit (Remote Employment Act 2021)
regimes.description: Permit for non-nationals working remotely in Grenada for employers or clients outside Grenada (Remote Employment Act, Act No. 3 of 2021); proof of actual annual income of at least EC$100,000 generated outside Grenada. Section 9(1): 'no income tax is payable in respect of any income generated by the non-national, or his or her dependant, outside of Grenada in accordance with this Act'. The Act is the instrument that lets the holder work remotely in Grenada (s.3(1)) while barring Grenadian clients and a local business (s.3(2)(b)); so 'income generated outside Grenada in accordance with this Act' is the foreign employer's or clients' pay for work done under the permit, and the exemption is read as covering work physically done in Grenada (covers_local_work true). Permit valid up to one year and renewable for further periods of up to one year (s.3(3), s.6); no cap on renewals is stated.
regimes.duration_note: Valid up to one year (s.3(3)); renewable for periods not exceeding one year (s.6) with the EC$100,000 income proof; the Act states no maximum number of renewals.

sources.title: Grenada Remote Employment Act, 2021 (Act No. 3 of 2021)
Stamped Nomad: Grenada Digital Nomad Visa (remote-work permit)

open_questions: Social security for permit holders is not addressed in the Act.

Interpretation: the wording 'generated outside of Grenada' is not defined; the reading that it covers remote work done while living in Grenada rests on the Act's purpose and on s.3, not on a definition or a tax-authority ruling.
EC$100,000 is about USD 37,000 at the XCD 2.70 peg.

income.residence_routes: Remote workers of any citizenship (other than Grenadian and OECS Protocol states) can use the one-year renewable remote-work permit (EC$100,000 income from abroad, health insurance, police certificate, USD 1,500). Employees of a Grenadian employer need a work permit under the Foreign Nationals and Commonwealth Citizens (Employment) Act (not researched). Citizenship by investment is a separate route (amounts not verified in data/jurisdictions/GRD.json). US citizens remain taxable in the US on worldwide income; Grenada does not tax foreign income of residents per Deloitte.

succession.name: Grenada
succession.summary: Grenada follows English-derived common law and no forced heirship was found. The International Trusts Act (1996) was amended in 2018 to stop new international trusts after 31 December 2018. No private foundation law was found and the Hague Trusts Convention is not in force.
succession.foreign_law_note: No source read states Grenada's conflict rule for a foreign national's estate. Common-law rule: movables follow the law of the domicile, land follows local law. Not confirmed in local statute for this jurisdiction.
succession.trust_note: Grenada is not in the HCCH status table. A news report says the International Trusts (Amendment) Act 2018 bars new international trusts from 31 December 2018; ordinary common-law trusts remain. No foundation statute found.
open_questions: No source read confirms Grenada has no forced heirship or family provision law.
The 2018 amendment was read only via a news report.
Whether a foundation statute exists was not confirmed.
Private foundations: no source found either way; not finding a foundation law is not evidence that there is none.

immigration.name: Grenada
immigration.summary: No free movement for anyone. Grenada citizenship costs USD 235,000 (National Transformation Fund, single applicant up to a family of four) or USD 270,000-350,000 in approved real estate, plus about USD 9,000 of application, due diligence, processing and interview fees. Grenada citizens can reportedly apply for the US E-2 treaty investor visa, the programme's main selling point; the programme is under an independent review announced 22 September 2026. Ordinary residence routes could not be sourced.
immigration.naturalisation: Ordinary naturalisation residence period not verified in this research; see open questions.
immigration.dual_citizenship_note: Dual citizenship is allowed for CBI citizens (not verified against the Citizenship Act this pass).

routes.name: Citizenship by Investment: National Transformation Fund (NTF)
routes.summary: A USD 235,000 non-refundable contribution covers a single applicant, a couple or a family of four and gives citizenship.
routes.requirements: USD 235,000 for the main applicant plus up to three dependants (since 1 July 2024); extra dependants beyond three USD 25,000 or USD 50,000 each, siblings USD 75,000 each. Fees per person 17+: application USD 1,500, due diligence USD 5,000 (the enquiries page elsewhere says USD 6,000), processing USD 1,500, interview USD 1,000. Applications only through licensed agents. Applicants refused a visa by a visa-free partner may be refused. Banned nationalities not found.
routes.investment_options: NTF USD 235,000; approved real estate USD 270,000 or USD 350,000 (official page unlabeled; secondary sources say fractional share vs full ownership).
routes.fees_note: 1,500 application + 5,000 due diligence + 1,500 processing + 1,000 interview. Passport and oath fees not sourced from IMA Grenada.
routes.physical_presence: None stated by IMA Grenada. One secondary source reports a 30-day-within-5-years rule announced for mid-2026; unverified.
routes.processing_time: IMA states approval within 60 business days of submission (subject to due diligence and receipt of funds).
routes.tax_note: Citizenship alone does not end tax residence elsewhere. Grenada citizens may use the US E-2 treaty visa (not verified against a US source).

routes.name: Citizenship by Investment: Approved real estate
routes.summary: Invest in an approved Grenada project (hotel, resort, villa) from USD 270,000, plus a USD 50,000 government fee.
routes.requirements: Approved project minimum shown as USD 350,000 / USD 270,000 on the IMA page without labels; government fee USD 50,000; application, due diligence, processing and interview fees as for the NTF. Holding period not stated on the page reached.
routes.fees_note: 50,000 government fee + 9,000 other fees, single applicant. Whether USD 270,000 is a fractional share (secondary sources) is unconfirmed.

Due diligence fee: USD 5,000 (application guide) vs USD 6,000 (enquiries page); which is current is unresolved.

Ordinary residence routes (retiree, permanent residence), a reported digital nomad scheme (Remote Employment Act: reported USD 1,500 fee, EC$100,000 income, 1 year; conflicting sources) and US E-2 treaty eligibility were not verified from official sources.
Ordinary naturalisation residence period not found.
ECCIRA start date: sources conflict (April 2026, Q2 2026, September 2026, 'late 2026', or not yet operational as of 8 August 2026). Check eccira.org.
